CruiseMapper currently has no ship schedule for Port Alkmaar (Netherlands North Holland)

Alkmaar (port locode NLALK) is a North Holland Canal (river) cruise port, city and municipality in the Netherlands's North Holland province, with population around 110,000. The closest to Alkmaar "cruise cities" are Hoorn (east) and IJmuiden (southwest).

The town is best-known among foreign and domestic tourists for its outdoor cheese market (open April through September on the Waagplein).

The settlement was founded in the 10th century and in 1254 received its city rights. In August-October 1573 (during the 80 Years War / 1568-1648 between Spain and the revolting Holland, Belgium, and Luxembourg) the town was sieged by Spanish forces. The town was interlinked via Noordhollandsch Kanaal (1824), Alkmaar-Den Helder railway (1865) and Alkmaar-Haarlem railway (1867). The A9 highway links with Amsterdam and Den Helder.

Noordhollandsch Kanaal (North-Holland Canal) has length approx 75 km (47 mi) and links Den Helder (north) with Amsterdam (south) via Alkmaar and Purmerend. This inland waterway was built (dug) in the period 1820-24 to shorten the sea access to Amsterdam City. However, due to vessels' increasing size (length, width, and draught) as well as the many bridges, sluices, and curves, the waterway soon became inadequate for seagoing ships. Plus, the canal's water freezes during the winter months. Noordzeekanaal (North Sea Canal) in 1865-76 linking directly Amsterdam with IJmuiden was built for this reason.

Today, the North Holland Canal is used exclusively for commercial river shipping, recreational boating (yachts, hotel barges, cruise ships, tour boats) and water management.

As a cruise port, Alkmaar is included in the regular schedule of one of Europe's largest river cruise companies - Nicko Cruises (brand of Mystic Cruises).

River cruise ships in Alkmaar berth directly in downtown. The town's 3 cruise docks can handle boats with max LOA lengths 130 m (Kanaalkade), 120 m (Noorderkade) and 90 m (Voormeer).

At a Glance

Easy independently. River cruise ships berth beside the northern and eastern edges of central Alkmaar, and the compact historic district is readily explored on foot. Most visitors can walk from the quay to Waagplein, the canals, museums and shopping streets without needing a shuttle or taxi.

Getting from the Cruise Berth

River vessels may use Kanaalkade, Noorderkade or Voormeer. Kanaalkade and Noorderkade are immediately beside the city center, while Voormeer is slightly farther east but remains within practical walking distance of the main sights. Alkmaar has simple quays rather than a large passenger terminal, so check the vessel's exact berth before setting out.

The historic center has mostly level streets, although cobblestones, narrow lanes and canal bridges can make wheelchair or mobility-aid access uneven. Taxis are more useful for trips outside Alkmaar than for sightseeing within the old town.

Best Ways to Spend Your Time

Historic Center and Waagplein

Allow 2–3 hours for a relaxed circuit through Waagplein, the narrow lanes around Fnidsen and Hekelstraat, the Mient canal, Langestraat and the Grote Kerk. This is the most practical choice for a short call and requires no transport.

Alkmaar Cheese Market

The traditional cheese market is held at Waagplein on selected mornings during the spring and summer season, with additional evening events on limited dates. It is a scheduled demonstration rather than a daily attraction, so verify that its date and time match the ship's call. Arrive early because the square can become crowded.

When the market is not operating, visitors can still see the historic Waag building and consider the Dutch Cheese Museum inside. The Alkmaar Store tourist office is also located at Waagplein.

Canal Boat Trip

A small sightseeing boat provides a different view of Alkmaar's façades, drawbridges and narrow canals. Standard trips take about 45 minutes and normally depart near the Waag area. Some bridges are extremely low, and passengers may need to bend down as the boat passes beneath them. Confirm departure times after reaching the center rather than relying on a boat trip for a tightly timed visit.

Museums and Grote Kerk

The Stedelijk Museum Alkmaar is the main choice for local art and city history. It stands near the Grote Kerk, making the two easy to combine in approximately 1.5–2.5 hours. The Dutch Cheese Museum at Waagplein is smaller and better suited to a brief visit. Check same-day opening before planning around either museum or the church.

Countryside, Windmills or the Coast

The polders, villages and North Sea coast around Alkmaar are better suited to a guided excursion, taxi tour or carefully planned bicycle trip. Possible regional destinations include the Schermer windmill landscape, De Rijp, Egmond aan Zee and the Schoorl dunes. These are not sensible additions to a very short call, and public-transport journeys require extra allowance for connections and delays.

Self-Guided Walking Tours

Easy Old Town Circuit

Distance: approximately 3 km (1.9 mi). Pure walking time: about 45 minutes. Recommended total time: 2–3 hours. Difficulty: easy, with occasional cobblestones and small canal bridges.

  1. Cruise quay: Walk toward the historic center from Kanaalkade, Noorderkade or Voormeer.
  2. Waagplein: See the Waag building and the setting of the seasonal cheese market.
  3. De Mient: Follow the canal past historic façades and waterside terraces.
  4. Fnidsen and Hekelstraat: Explore the compact old-quarter lanes and independent shops.
  5. Langestraat: Cross the principal pedestrian shopping street toward the Grote Kerk.
  6. Grote Kerk: View the large late-Gothic church and nearby cultural quarter.
  7. Return: Walk through the center to the appropriate quay, allowing time to locate the correct vessel entrance.

Extended Monuments and Canals Walk

Distance: approximately 4.5 km (2.8 mi). Pure walking time: about 1 hour. Recommended total time: 2.5–3.5 hours. Difficulty: easy to moderate because of the longer distance, cobbles and bridges.

  1. Begin at the cruise quay and continue to Waagplein.
  2. Walk through the old lanes around Fnidsen and the Visbanken.
  3. Continue toward the Accijnstoren beside the water.
  4. Follow the green edge of the old center toward Molen van Piet.
  5. Visit the Grote Kerk and adjacent museum quarter.
  6. Return through Langestraat and the Mient canal area to the ship.

This route follows the character of Alkmaar's official monuments walk. A route description or city map may be available from the tourist office in the Waag.

Practical Tips

  • Confirm the vessel's berth name, as Alkmaar has several river-cruise mooring areas.
  • Wear shoes suitable for cobblestones and canal bridges.
  • Check the cheese-market calendar before making it the focus of the visit.
  • Reserve a canal cruise only if its finishing time leaves a comfortable margin.
  • For independent regional trips, allow extra time for bicycle returns, traffic or public-transport connections.
  • Plan to be back at the quay well before the ship's stated all-aboard time.
